title: Teng
capsule: Teng was a small Zhou vassal state in southern Shandong, traditionally founded after the conquest of Shang (c. 1046 BCE) by Shu Xiu of Cuo, a younger brother of King Wu of Zhou, and ruled thereafter by his Ji-clan descendants. Nominally subordinate to its larger neighbor Lu, the state occupied the territory of modern Tengzhou and is remembered as the homeland of the philosopher Mozi and the legendary craftsman Lu Ban. During the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods it survived as a minor power among aggressive neighbors; it was first overrun by the state of Yue around 414 BCE, briefly restored by its nobility, and finally annihilated by King Kang of Song around 297 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general territory around Tengzhou is secure from textual sources and the survival of the place-name; the exact boundaries of Teng's territory at any period are undocumented.
